newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen steady at the open, then cautious.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen steady at the open, then cautious.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were seen holding steady with a mild upward bias at the market open on Thursday, but investors were expected to be cautious ahead of tomorrow's key U.S. unemployment data, analysts said.

The stock market could get an initial lift from short-covering and as bargain hunters searched for buying opportunities among technology sector, recently battered by several profit warnings, one analyst said.
But trading could then settle, with markets unsure what unemployment data would mean for U.S. interest rates.

"The market remains somewhat cautious although it looks like we're set for a slightly higher opening," Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments said. "The highlight will be tomorrow's unemployment report."

U.S. nonfarm payrolls, which were due out at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT on Friday, were expected to be up 219,000 in May versus a previous 142,000 rise. The unemployment rate was expected to be five percent in May compared to a previous 4.9 percent.
Stronger-than-expected data could give new life to lurking fears that the Federal Reserve will raise U.S. interest rates in order to keep inflation at bay, analysts said.
"It could be a rocky session tomorrow but today we will be in a cautious trading range," Cardillo said.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was off 2/32 at a 6.89 percent yield and the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was up 1.55 points at 843.65.
On Wednesday, the Dow industrials finished down 42.49 points at 7269.66. The Nasdaq composite was hurt by pressure on technology issues and ended down 5.24 points at 1379.67.
Analysts said bargain hunting could boost technology shares on Thursday, but the sector remained sensitive to all company and industry commentary during the session.
"Right now, techs look like they are leaning higher," Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities said. "After that, it will depend on commentary and trends during the day."
On Thursday, the stock market was hit by worries that personal computer makers were suffering from declining demand and would issue profit warnings.

Japan's Nikkei-225 index finished off 123.41 points at 20488.15. In London, the FTSE 100 was up 1.9 points at 4559. U.S. stocks were steady there as many European investors stayed on the sidelines before U.S. unemployment data.
The dollar slipped against the yen in Tokyo, trading at 115.87/92 yen. In Europe, the dollar at 1.7285/95 marks.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column said troubles at U.S. retailer Kmart Corp might not be over, according to some analysts. Wall Street analysts expect the company to report May same-store sales grew as little as 2.5 percent, well below its plan of four to six percent.

The New York Times said in its Market Place column that while Microsoft Corp executives have cautioned that the company's growth could slow and that multiples were too high, the share price remains strong.
